story.description: Build a reusable, authorable introductory content block for the homepage area titled DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED. The captured content includes a video area, playback helper text, the page theme heading, and two interactive calls to action: PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE. Detailed typography, color values, pixel spacing, hover behavior, video source, poster image, transcript, and duration were not captured and must remain configurable rather than hardcoded.
accessibilityCriteria: The video interaction supports keyboard operation using Enter or Space, matching the captured playback instruction.
Both calls to action expose clear accessible names matching their visible labels: PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE.

implementationAnalysis.rationale: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded 'Hero Video' block (componentId: component-001, canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo) with a four-cell single-row table structure. The authored table header is 'Hero Video' and the single row contains four cells: [video asset], [heading text], [primary CTA link], [secondary CTA link]. The live page confirms the block renders at div.herovideo with computed rect {x:0, y:64, width:780, height:438.75} — a full-width video hero immediately below the header. The section-metadata for this section supplies subtitles, poster, and transcript as section-level configuration (not block-row cells), which is consistent with EDS section-metadata conventions and must be preserved. The block does not exist in the repository inventory (blocks/ contains: cards, columns, footer, fragment, header, hero, widget — no hero-video). Therefore a new block must be created at blocks/hero-video/hero-video.js and blocks/hero-video/hero-video.css. The JS decorator must: (1) read the four authored cells — video link/asset, heading, primary CTA anchor, secondary CTA anchor; (2) build a native HTML5 <video> element using the video cell href as src, with poster/subtitles sourced from section-metadata on the parent section element (keys: poster, subtitles, transcript) so they remain configurable; (3) render the heading as an <h1> or <h2> (the live page shows the herovideo block text includes the heading inline, not as a separate DOM heading, so the decorator must promote it); (4) render the two CTA anchors with their captured accessible aria-label values (aria-label='PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and aria-label='LEARN MORE about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' are present in the live computed samples — the decorator must set aria-label on each anchor using the heading text appended to the link label, matching the live pattern); (5) support keyboard play/pause via Enter and Space on the video element, matching the captured helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' and the accessibility criterion; (6) render a visually-hidden helper text element containing that exact string for screen-reader context. The CSS must not hardcode color, typography, spacing, hover, or animation values that were listed as uncaptured — only structural layout rules (position, display, width) are safe to author. The section-metadata block (style: full-width, video-container; subtitles; poster; transcript) is already grounded in the Content Agent document and must be read by the JS decorator from the parent section's dataset or child section-metadata block — no new section-metadata authoring is required. The Cards (overlay) block (component-002) is a separate block in the same section and is out of scope for this story.

filePlan.reason: New block decorator. Reads the four authored table cells (video asset link, heading, primary CTA anchor, secondary CTA anchor) from the EDS-decorated block DOM (each cell is a div > div). Reads section-metadata keys poster, subtitles, and transcript from the parent section element's dataset (EDS decorateSections writes section-metadata key/value pairs as data-* attributes on the section div) to keep those values configurable. Builds a

New block stylesheet. Provides only structural layout rules: .hero-video position:relative, full-width video element (width:100%, display:block), overlay div positioned absolute over the video, visually-hidden utility class for the helper text paragraph (position:absolute, width:1px, height:1px, overflow:hidden, clip), and CTA anchor display:inline-block. Does not hardcode color, background, font-family, font-size, font-weight, letter-spacing, line-height, border-radius, padding, hover transitions, or animation values — all of which were listed as uncaptured in the evidence and must remain configurable by the project's style system or future authored tokens.

assumptions: The Content Agent authored table for Hero Video has exactly one data row with four cells in order: [video asset/link], [heading text], [primary CTA anchor], [secondary CTA anchor]. The table header row contains only 'Hero Video'. This is inferred from the componentId component-001 field model (video, heading, primaryAction, secondaryAction) and the sourceText '/assets/media_1d23079eb9b89c419b9e761a06135ae666a271db9.mp4 DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED PLAY FULL VIDEO LEARN MORE'. The nested object cells in the finalAuthoringContract table rows are not expanded in the JSON but the field model and sourceText confirm this four-cell order.

EDS decorateSections writes section-metadata key/value pairs as data-* attributes on the section element (e.g., data-poster, data-subtitles, data-transcript, data-style). The hero-video.js decorator reads these from block.closest('.section').dataset. If the project's decorateSections does not write section-metadata to dataset, the decorator will fall back to querying the section-metadata block's rows directly.

The video source cell in the authored table contains a link element whose href resolves to the mp4 file. The captured sourceText shows the partial path /assets/media_1d23079eb9b89c419b9e761a06135ae666a271db9.mp4 — the decorator will use the anchor's resolved href attribute as the video src.

The 'Video' text visible in the block's computed text content ('Video Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.') is the accessible label for the video element, not a separate authored text node. It will be set as aria-label='Video' on the <video> element.

The PLAY FULL VIDEO link (href='#fullscreen-cta') triggers a fullscreen or modal video experience. The decorator renders it as a standard anchor; any fullscreen behavior is out of scope for this story and must be implemented separately.

The section-metadata style values 'full-width' and 'video-container' are applied as CSS classes on the section element by EDS's section decoration logic. The hero-video block CSS does not need to re-implement full-width behavior — it relies on the section's full-width class removing the default max-width constraint from the wrapper div.
risks: Section-metadata dataset key names: EDS boilerplate decorateSections does not automatically parse section-metadata blocks into dataset attributes in the standard aem.js provided in this repository. The hero-video.js decorator must include a fallback that reads section-metadata by querying the .section-metadata block's rows directly if dataset keys are absent. This adds complexity but is safe.

Video autoplay policy: Modern browsers block autoplay of unmuted video without user interaction. The decorator sets muted=true and autoplay=true (matching the live site's likely behavior for a background hero video). If the authored intent is a non-autoplaying video, the poster image will display until the user activates play — this is acceptable and accessible.

The video source path /assets/media_1d23079eb9b89c419b9e761a06135ae666a271db9.mp4 is a partial path from the live Disney site and is not available in the boilerplate repository. Authors must supply a valid video URL in the authored document. The decorator must not hardcode this path.

The four-cell table structure is inferred from the field model and sourceText because the finalAuthoringContract table rows show '[nested object omitted]' for cells 1, 3, and 4. If the actual authored structure differs (e.g., video and heading in the same cell, or CTAs in a single cell as two anchors), the decorator's cell-index assumptions will need adjustment. The implementation should be defensive and use querySelector within each cell rather than strict index assumptions.

The repository uses the boilerplate's standard decorateButtons which buttonizes anchors wrapped in <strong> or <em>. If the authored CTAs are wrapped in strong/em, they will receive button classes from decorateButtons before hero-video.js runs. The decorator should handle both raw anchors and button-classed anchors in the CTA cells.

No existing herovideo block exists in the repository, so there is no risk of regression to existing block behavior. However, the live site loads /blocks/herovideo/herovideo.css (note: no hyphen in 'herovideo' on the live site). The EDS canonical block name derived from the authored table header 'Hero Video' is 'hero-video' (with hyphen, per toClassName). The repository block folder must be named hero-video to match EDS conventions, which differs from the live site's herovideo folder name. This is correct for the migration target repository.
